question: Can an existing calibrated receive route bridge1000-1710MHz?
findings: Current PAC original coefficient helper and compiled C agree for30 synthetic contexts across10 working frequencies spanning1000.0001-1710.7MHz; no coefficient wrap in these points. Working frequency is not RF reception.
B3 software floor1710MHz is an explicit profile envelope, not a check inside the tested coefficient helper. Below1805MHz its initialization anchor remains channel1200/1805MHz.
B3 uses selector2/port1, while B5 selector4/port2 and B8 selector6/port3. Shared B-bank arithmetic does not imply shared analog passband.

B prepare uses field4 from NV RX port to select analog row0x8a54+10*port. Named calibration callback at0x5354 targets0x453c and applies selector/slot/context tables; it does not read request frequency or ready/VCO. This is table application, not an unresolved autonomous calibration routine.
Original1447-1466.9MHz rows45/61 use selector18 but recorded SDK route checks have no matching NV or RX port. They cannot be enabled by bypassing calibration gates.

Focused original/C request composition at1100/1447/1600/1710MHz acrossBW0-BW5 passes at-O0/-O2 using recorded B3/B5/B8 routes and NV. B3 post-RX helper0x38a8 has24 focused cases; all select the same default register profile. These executions use retained SDK RF image and historical board NV, not live RF RAM or current PAC full caller proof.
decision: Software evidence now supports a bounded B3 test extension while preserving selector2,port1 and valid channel1200/1805MHz anchor. It does not support unrestricted Auto coverage. First candidate should expose a controlled representative point, retain NV gate and stop/drain, and require reference on/off plus retune follow before promotion.
next: Build a bounded experimental B3 lower-envelope candidate using the common profile table, preserving NV/anchor and existing baseline. Validate AP/CP/host bounds and packaging; user manual flash. Start with one representative just below1710MHz and a known1710MHz control; stop expansion if reference identification fails without changed conditions.
